Observations

course_amt <- uw_grades_df |>
  pull(Course_Number) |> 
  unique() |> 
  length()

There are 9123 courses in this dataset.

GPA_avg <- uw_grades_df |>
  pull(Average_GPA) |>
  mean(na.rm = TRUE) |>
  round(2)

The Average of the average GPAs is 3.41.

Student_avg <- uw_grades_df |>
  pull(Student_Count) |>
  mean(na.rm = TRUE) |>
  round(2)

The average amount of students per course is 45.38.

min_course_num <- uw_grades_df |>
  pull(Course_Number_Num) |>
  min()

The lowest course number is 100.

max_course_num <- uw_grades_df |>
  pull(Course_Number_Num) |>
  max()

The highest course number is 750.

ggplot(uw_grades_df) +
  geom_histogram(
    mapping = aes(
      x = Average_GPA, binwidth = .1 ), fill = "blue"
  )+
  
  labs(
    title = "Average GPA", x = "GPA", y = "frequency"
  )
ggplot(uw_grades_df) +
  geom_point(
    mapping = aes(
      x = Student_Count, y = Average_GPA), fill = "red"
  )+
  
  labs(
    title = "Average GPA Scatterplot", x = "Student Count", y = "Average GPA"
  )

From the data, we can see that there are a total of 9123 courses and on average, there are 45.38 average students in each class. The average GPA across all courses is also relatively high at 3.41. The lowest course number is 100 and the highest course number is 750. This is very interesting because the higher these courses go, it may imply that the difficulty gets harder and it could mean that students struggle and bring the average GPA down because of those classes. The histogram shows how the average GPAs of students stays around 3.5 for most people. The scatterplot also shows this but it also shows some outliers where some people have close to a 2 GPA.

Comparisons

Difference in Academic Year averages in 2014 and 2015

gpa_data_2014 <- uw_grades_df |> 
  filter(Academic_Year == "2013-14")

gpa_data_2015 <- uw_grades_df |> 
  filter(Academic_Year == "2014-15")

max_course_num_2015 <- gpa_data_2015 |>
  pull(Course_Number_Num) |>
  max()

max_course_num_2014 <- gpa_data_2014 |>
  pull(Course_Number_Num) |>
  max()

GPA_avg_2014 <- gpa_data_2014 |>
  pull(Average_GPA) |>
  mean(na.rm = TRUE) |>
  round(2)

GPA_avg_2015 <- gpa_data_2015 |>
  pull(Average_GPA) |>
  mean(na.rm = TRUE) |>
  round(2)
ggplot(gpa_data_2014) +
  geom_point(
    mapping = aes(x = Student_Count, y = Average_GPA), 
    color = "red"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "All Average GPAs for 2014", 
    x = "Student Count", 
    y = "Average GPA"
  )
ggplot(gpa_data_2015) +
  geom_point(
    mapping = aes(x = Student_Count, y = Average_GPA), 
    color = "blue"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "All Average GPAs for 2015", 
    x = "Student Count", 
    y = "Average GPA"
  )
ggplot(gpa_data_2014) +
  geom_histogram(
    mapping = aes(x = Average_GPA), 
    fill = "red", binwidth = 0.1) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of All GPAs for 2014", 
    x = "Average GPA", y = "Count of Class Sections")
ggplot(gpa_data_2015) +
  geom_histogram(
    mapping = aes(x = Average_GPA), 
    fill = "blue", binwidth = 0.1) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of All GPAs for 2015", 
    x = "Average GPA", y = "Count of Class Sections")

For both 2015 and 2014, the GPAs are around the same average. The max course number for 2014 was 750 and was 699 for 2015. The average GPA for 2014 was 3.42 and was 3.43 for 2015.

Comparison 2

Difference in averages from Instructor KNOWLEN, CARL and FERRANTE, ANTONINO

gpa_data_KC <- uw_grades_df |> 
  filter(Primary_Instructor == "FERRANTE, ANTONINO")

gpa_data_FA <- uw_grades_df |> 
  filter(Primary_Instructor == "KNOWLEN, CARL")

max_course_num_KC <- gpa_data_KC |>
  pull(Course_Number_Num) |>
  max()

max_course_num_FA <- gpa_data_FA |>
  pull(Course_Number_Num) |>
  max()

GPA_avg_KC <- gpa_data_KC |>
  pull(Average_GPA) |>
  mean(na.rm = TRUE) |>
  round(2)

GPA_avg_FA <- gpa_data_FA |>
  pull(Average_GPA) |>
  mean(na.rm = TRUE) |>
  round(2)
ggplot(gpa_data_KC) +
  geom_point(
    mapping = aes(x = Student_Count, y = Average_GPA), 
    color = "red"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "All Average GPAs for KNOWLEN, CARL", 
    x = "Student Count", 
    y = "Average GPA"
  )
ggplot(gpa_data_FA) +
  geom_point(
    mapping = aes(x = Student_Count, y = Average_GPA), 
    color = "blue"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "All Average GPAs for FERRANTE, ANTONINO", 
    x = "Student Count", 
    y = "Average GPA"
  )
ggplot(gpa_data_KC) +
  geom_histogram(
    mapping = aes(x = Average_GPA), 
    fill = "red", binwidth = 0.1) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of All GPAs for KNOWLEN, CARL", 
    x = "Average GPA", y = "Count of Course Numbers")
ggplot(gpa_data_FA) +
  geom_histogram(
    mapping = aes(x = Average_GPA), 
    fill = "blue", binwidth = 0.1) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of All GPAs for FERRANTE, ANTONINO", 
    x = "Average GPA", y = "Count of Course Numbers")

For both CARL KNOWLEN and ANTONINO FERRANTE, the GPAs are very different because of the difficulty of classes. The max course number for CARL KNOWLEN was 598 and was 532 for ANTONINO FERRANTE. The average GPA for CARL KNOWLEN was 3.38 and was 3.31 for ANTONINO FERRANTE. This shows that ANTONINO FERRANTE’s classes are a bit harder than CARL KNOWLEN’s classes. This also shows that the course number is not really relevant because even though CARL KNOWLEN’s class number is higher than ANTONINO FERRANTE’s, the GPA’s indicate that the lower course number is harder.
